bug_semantics: In the Git node clone operation, n8n resolved and checked the workflow-supplied repositoryPath against restricted paths, then later performed filesystem operations and invoked git using that pathname. An authenticated workflow user could replace a checked directory or ancestor with a symlink during the check/use interval. The git subprocess then followed the new link and cloned an attacker-controlled repository into n8n's restricted data/community-node area. On restart, n8n loaded the planted custom JavaScript node, producing server-side arbitrary code execution.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructed code commit is PR member 8a83f6a9c5dd3b64b0ec940a8206d812ffe32c21. It introduced the security check `await this.helpers.isFilePathBlocked(repositoryPath)` in packages/nodes-base/nodes/Git/Git.node.ts before the pre-existing clone path use, but did not bind subsequent mkdir/git operations to the object that had been checked. That created the advisory's TOCTOU check/use gap. The member was squash-landed as a49b179e891c0b3501b6784c82af72b5a8c5a02d; later commits changed path resolution and clone spelling without removing the race.
